title: Connexions de Gauss-Manin et équations de Picard-Fuchs. Opération de Cartier : copies de tapuscrit annoté (s.d.), tiré à part (1981), notes manuscrites (s.d.).

deep.reconstruction:
Setting: a relative situation S → T. Grothendieck is preparing a description of differential operators defined on horizontal and closed objects. This feeds the next page and the Gauss–Manin / Picard–Fuchs programme of the dossier: differential operators on quotients M = E/N, i.e. Picard–Fuchs-type equations satisfied by classes. Notation: Diff^i(A,B) = Hom_O(P^i(A), B), where P^i is the sheaf of principal parts of order i.

(1) Let F →D→ G →D'→ H be differential operators. Implicitly D and D' have order 1, because the order shifts by 1 at each step. Suppose the sequence is 'formally exact', meaning the induced sequences of jets/linearizations are exact. Then for every P two sequences are exact:
- Diff^i(P,F) → Diff^{i+1}(P,G) → Diff^{i+2}(P,H), via u ↦ D∘u and v ↦ D'∘v.
- Dually, Diff^i(H,P) → Diff^{i+1}(G,P) → Diff^{i+2}(F,P), via composition on the right.
In modern terms: formal exactness means the linearized complex D_{S/T}⊗F → D⊗G → D⊗H is filtered-exact. One then applies Hom, which needs local splitting of the filtered pieces. Grothendieck boxed this part with 'à revoir'.

(2) Let E be a locally free stratified O_S-module, i.e. a module with an integrable connection (or HPD-stratification). Assume the formal Poincaré lemma holds for the de Rham complex Ω^•_{S/T}(E). An example is S smooth over T in characteristic 0. Then for every quasi-coherent P and every i ≥ 0 the following sequence is exact:
0 ← Hom(E,P) ← Diff^i(E,P) ← Diff^{i-1}(E⊗Ω^1,P) ← Diff^{i-2}(E⊗Ω^2,P) ← …
- The maps after the first are u ↦ u∘d^0_E, u ↦ u∘d^1_E, and so on.
- The first map sends u ∈ Hom(P^i(E),P) to u∘δ^E_i, where δ^E_i : E → P^i(E) is the map given by the stratification.
This is the order-filtered Hom-dual of the linearized de Rham complex E⊗P^∞⊗Ω^•. Equivalently, it is the filtered Spencer resolution of E twisted by the connection.

The NB defines Diff^i_+(E,P) as the kernel of Diff^i(E,P) → Hom(E,P). These are the operators 'with constant coefficients relative to the stratification'.

The next page draws the consequences. Diff_+ is identified with Diff^{i-1}(E⊗Ω^1,P) modulo the image of Diff^{i-2}(E⊗Ω^2,P). This injects into additive maps Ker d^1_E → P, which defines 'differential operators on the closed forms'. It is then applied to a submodule N ⊂ E and M = E/N, aimed at Picard–Fuchs type equations.
errors: Part (1) leaves 'formally exact' undefined and does not state that D and D' have order 1. The shift i → i+1 → i+2 only makes sense for first-order operators.

Exactness after applying Hom(-,P), or Hom(P,-), needs the order-filtered pieces of the linearized sequence to be exact and locally split. Without this the statement can fail. Grothendieck's boxed 'à revoir' acknowledges the gap.

In part (2) exactness in positive characteristic fails with ordinary principal parts. The Koszul/de Rham pieces are not exact there (Cartier phenomenon), hence the restriction to characteristic 0, or one would need PD-differential operators. The note implicitly recognizes this.

ideas.what: Exactness of the induced sequences of spaces of differential operators from a formally exact sequence of differential operators
ideas.modern_name: Linearization of differential operators; formal (Spencer) exactness and its Hom-dual
ideas.usually_credited_to: Spencer, Goldschmidt, Malgrange (1960s); linearization in Grothendieck–Berthelot crystalline theory
ideas.where_published: Grothendieck, 'Crystals and the de Rham cohomology of schemes' (Dix exposés, 1968), linearization of differential operators; developed in Berthelot's Cohomologie cristalline (LNM 407)

ideas.what: Filtered resolution 0 ← Hom(E,P) ← Diff^i(E,P) ← Diff^{i-1}(E⊗Ω^1,P) ← … for a stratified locally free E under the formal Poincaré lemma
ideas.modern_name: Filtered Spencer resolution / dual of the linearized de Rham complex of a module with integrable connection
ideas.usually_credited_to: Spencer; Grothendieck (1968); Berthelot (1974); standard in D-module theory (e.g. Kashiwara, Saito's filtered Spencer complex)
ideas.where_published: Crystals and de Rham cohomology (formal Poincaré lemma, linearization)

ideas.what: Diff_+(E,P): operators of order ≤ i vanishing on the horizontal part, 'à coefficients constants rel. à la stratification'
ideas.modern_name: Differential operators modulo O-linear part; operators factoring through the de Rham differential

deep.surprise_reason: This is standard homological bookkeeping on differential operators (linearization, formal Poincaré lemma, filtered Spencer resolution), all in Grothendieck–Berthelot crystalline theory and later D-module theory. It is preparatory to the Picard–Fuchs discussion on the next page. Nothing here seems absent from the literature.
transcription_corrections: Top-left label is more likely '[situation relative]' than '[lisse ?] relatif]'.
Boxed marginal note reads 'à revoir]' with no further illegible word needed.
In (2) the crossed label over the first arrow is 'ε(u)'. It is replaced by the bracketed description u ↦ u∘δ^E_i via Hom(P^i(E),P).
